pr_comments: Nice, glad to see it in the standard sidekiq setup :heart:
Hey @mperham, it's great to see sidekiq leveraging sd_notify. I'm curious, how come you didn't use the actual gem instead? Would be interested to know the reasoning. Thanks!

@agis The actual implementation is one .rb file and quite simple. I prefer to minimize 3rd party dependencies as it makes long-term maintenance much easier. Notice that Sidekiq only depends on the `rack` and `redis` gems (and connection_pool but that's my gem too).

issue_context.title: Add systemd notify and watchdog support
issue_context.body:
As Sidekiq is meant to be a long-running daemon, it should support the notification and watchdog functionality that systemd allows.

* [x] Add READY=1 notification upon startup
* [x] Add STOPPING=1 notification upon terminate
* [x] Add WATCHDOG=1 loop

See also https://github.com/agis/ruby-sdnotify
https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/sd_notify.html
comments: Can you please clarify whether this works with `sidekiqswarm`? It's not clear from the docs/changes
Right now it is only designed to work when running single process. If you want to open an issue, I’d be happy to get it working in swarm.
